records.text: Judas fell, and the rest fled.
Jonathan and Simon took up Judas their brother and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modein.
They wept for him, and all Israel lamented him with a great lament. They mourned for many days and said,
“How has the mighty one fallen, the saviour of Israel!”
After the death of Judas, the lawless emerged throughout all Israel’s territory, and all who practiced injustice rose up.
In those days an exceedingly great famine occurred, and the country went over to their side.
we have taken thought for the pleasure of those who wish to read, for the ease of those eager to commit it to memory, and for the benefit of everyone who encounters it.
For us who have undertaken the hard work of abridgement, the task is not easy; it involves sweat and sleeplessness.
Just as it is not easy for someone preparing a banquet and seeking others’ benefit, nevertheless, for the gratitude of the many, we will gladly bear the hard work.
We leave the precise treatment of each matter to the historian, while labouring to follow the outlines of the abridgement.

For just as the architect of a new house must consider its whole foundation, while the person undertaking its encaustic work and painting must examine what is suitable for decoration, so, I think, it is with us.
To enter deeply into matters, range widely in the discussion, and investigate the particulars belongs to the original historian.
But the person making a recasting should be permitted to pursue concise expression and set aside an exhaustive treatment of the subject.
Let us therefore begin the narrative here, adding only this much to what has already been said: it would be foolish to expand the preface to the history while abridging the history itself.
This is the copy of the letters Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
“Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders of the nation, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, to the Spartans their brothers, greetings.
In former times letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areus, who reigned among you, stating that you are our brothers, as the copy below shows.
Onias received the envoy with honour and accepted the letters, in which alliance and friendship were declared.
Although we have no need of these things, since we have as encouragement the holy books that are in our hands,
we have undertaken to send to renew brotherhood and friendship with you, so that we may not become estranged from you. For many seasons have passed since you sent to us.
We rejoice in your glory.
But many afflictions and many wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have made war on us.
We did not wish to trouble you or our other allies and friends in these wars,
for we have help from Heaven helping us; we were rescued from our enemies, and our enemies were humbled.
We have therefore chosen Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason and sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.
We have also commanded them to go to you, greet you, and deliver our letters concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.
Now you will do well to answer us concerning these matters.”
Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace.
He sent the children and the hundred talents, but Tryphon proved false and did not release Jonathan.
After this Tryphon came to invade the country and crush it. They went around by the road to Adora. Simon and his army moved opposite him wherever he went.
Those in the citadel sent envoys to Tryphon, urging him to come to them through the wilderness and send them food.
When he approached Bascama, he killed Jonathan, and Jonathan was buried there.
Tryphon turned and went away to his own land.
In what land does light lodge, and what is the place of darkness,
if you could lead Me to their boundaries, and if you also know their paths?
I know, then, that you were born at that time, and the number of your years is great.
From where does frost come out, or the south wind scatter beneath heaven?
Who prepared a flow for violent rain and a path for tumult,
to rain upon land where there is no man, a wilderness where no human exists,
to fill untrodden and uninhabited ground and make a growth of green plants sprout?
Who is the father of rain, and who gave birth to lumps of dew?
From whose belly does ice come forth, and who gave birth to frost in heaven,
which descends like flowing water? And who fixed the face of the abyss?
and that the Jews and priests had agreed that Simon should be their leader and high priest for ever, until a faithful prophet should arise;
that he should be their general, and take care of the holy places, appointing through his authority those in charge of their works, the country, the weapons, and the strongholds;
that he should take care of the holy places, be obeyed by everyone, have all documents in the country written in his name, and wear purple and gold ornaments;

and that no one among the people or priests should have authority to annul any of these things, contradict what he should say, convene a gathering in the country without him, wear purple, or fasten on a golden clasp.
All the people agreed to establish Simon to act according to these terms.
Simon accepted and agreed to serve as high priest, to be general and ethnarch of the Jews and priests, and to preside over them all.
They directed that this inscription be placed on bronze tablets and that these be set up within the enclosure of the holy places in a conspicuous place,
with three courses of strong stone and one wooden course. The expense will be paid from the king’s house.

And let the silver and gold vessels of God’s house, which Nabouchodonosor took from the house in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, be given back and go to the sanctuary in Jerusalem, to the place where they were set in God’s house.”
“Now you shall give, governors beyond the river, Satharbouzana and their fellow slaves the Apharsachaians beyond the river; keeping far away from there,
leave the work on God’s house alone. Let the leaders of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build that house of God on its site.

I have also issued a decision: for anyone who changes this word, a timber will be taken down from his house, and he will be raised upright and fastened upon it. His house will be dealt with according to me.

The God whose name dwells there will overthrow every king and people who stretches out a hand to alter or destroy that house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued the decision; it shall be carried out diligently.”
On the second day King Antiochus encamped against Dora, continually bringing his forces against it, making siege engines, and blocking Tryphon from going out or coming in.
Simon sent him two thousand picked men to fight alongside him, along with silver, gold, and ample equipment.
He would not receive them, but annulled everything he had previously agreed with Simon and became estranged from him.
He sent Athenobius, one of his Friends, to confer with him, saying, “You hold Joppa, Gazara, and the citadel in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom.
You have devastated their territories, inflicted a great blow upon the land, and gained control of many places in my kingdom.
Now, therefore, hand over the cities you have seized and the tribute of the places you have taken outside the borders of Judea.

Otherwise, give five hundred talents of silver in their place, and another five hundred talents for the destruction you have caused and the tribute of the cities. If not, we will come and make war on you.”
Simon answered him, “We have neither taken foreign land nor gained control of others’ property, but the inheritance of our fathers, which our enemies unjustly seized at one time.
Now that we have the opportunity, we are holding fast to the inheritance of our fathers.
As for Joppa and Gazara, which you demand, these caused a great blow among the people and in our country. For these we will give a hundred talents.”
He did not answer him a word, but returned angrily to the king and reported these words, Simon’s glory, and everything he had seen. The king became greatly angry.
The queen of Sheba heard Solomon’s name and the Lord’s name, and came to test him with riddles.
She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices, very much gold, and precious stones. She came in to Solomon and spoke to him about everything in her heart.
Solomon explained all her matters to her. No matter was overlooked by the king that he did not explain to her.
She gave Solomon a hundred twenty talents of gold, very many spices, and precious stones. Never again came such an abundance of spices as the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
Hiram’s ship, which carried gold from Souphir, also brought a very great quantity of unhewn wood and precious stones.

The king made the unhewn wood into supports for the Lord’s house and the king’s house, and into harps and lyres for the singers. No such unhewn wood has come upon the earth or been seen anywhere to this day.

King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired and asked for, besides everything he had given her through King Solomon’s hand. Then she returned and went to her land, she and all her attendants.
Now I release you and exempt all the Jews from tribute, the salt charge, and crown payments.
